person: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Geoffrey Hinton
role: Deep learning researchers, University of Toronto (Hinton: cognitive psychologist/computer scientist, not a neuroscientist)
title: AlexNet wins ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012)
summary: A GPU-trained convolutional neural network won the ImageNet challenge with a 15.3% top-5 error, more than 10.8 points ahead of the runner-up, igniting the deep learning era.

person: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio
role: Machine learning researchers, Université de Montréal / MILA
title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
summary: Introduced the attention mechanism for neural machine translation, letting a model learn which source words to focus on; the direct ancestor of the Transformer.

role: Philosopher, Future of Humanity Institute, Oxford
title: Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies
summary: Systematic argument that a machine superintelligence could rapidly outstrip humans and that solving the 'control problem' must precede it; the book moved AI existential risk into mainstream debate.

role: Entrepreneur (Tesla, SpaceX); later OpenAI co-founder
title: 'Summoning the demon' remarks, MIT AeroAstro Centennial Symposium (Oct 2014)
summary: Musk called AI probably humanity's biggest existential threat and urged national and international regulatory oversight.
quote: With artificial intelligence we are summoning the demon. In all those stories where there's the guy with the pentagram and the holy water, it's like – yeah, he's sure he can control the demon. Doesn't work out.

role: Theoretical physicist, Cambridge
title: BBC interview: AI 'could spell the end of the human race' (Dec 2014)
summary: Hawking warned that full AI could take off on its own and redesign itself at an ever-increasing rate, superseding slowly evolving humans.
quote: The development of full artificial intelligence could spell the end of the human race.

person: Future of Life Institute (Max Tegmark et al.; signed by Russell, Hawking, Musk, Hassabis and thousands more)
role: Research community open letter, after the Puerto Rico 'Future of AI' conference (Jan 2015)
title: Research Priorities for Robust and Beneficial Artificial Intelligence: An Open Letter
summary: The first mass statement from mainstream AI researchers that AI safety research deserved attention, attaching a research-priorities agenda.
quote: our AI systems must do what we want them to do.

role: Philosopher, Future of Humanity Institute, Oxford
title: TED2015: What happens when our computers get smarter than we are?
summary: Bostrom argued machine intelligence will race past human level and that values must be instilled before, not after, the transition.
quote: The train doesn't stop at Humanville Station. It's likely, rather, to swoosh right by.

role: Chief Scientist, Baidu; Stanford; Google Brain co-founder
title: GTC 2015 keynote: killer robots vs. 'overpopulation on Mars'
summary: Ng dismissed evil superintelligence as 'an unnecessary distraction', the classic skeptic position of the era.
quote: I don't work on not turning AI evil today for the same reason I don't worry about the problem of overpopulation on the planet Mars.

role: Co-founder and CEO, DeepMind; PhD in cognitive neuroscience (UCL)
title: Google Zeitgeist: Human AI is decades away, but we need to start the debate now
summary: Hassabis framed DeepMind's mission as neuroscience-inspired general learning via reinforcement learning, while urging an early ethics debate.
quote: Although human-level, general artificial intelligence is many decades away, I think we should start the debate now.

person: DeepMind (Demis Hassabis, David Silver) vs. Lee Sedol
role: AI lab vs. 9-dan Go professional
title: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol 4–1 (Seoul, March 2016); Move 37
summary: AlphaGo's 37th move in game 2, a shoulder hit few professionals would consider, was hailed as 'creative' and became the emblem of machine intuition; the 2017 documentary 'AlphaGo' records the match.

person: Dario Amodei, Chris Olah, Jacob Steinhardt, Paul Christiano, John Schulman, Dan Mané
role: Researchers at Google Brain, OpenAI, Stanford, UC Berkeley
title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
summary: Reframed safety as engineering: five practical research problems on 'accidents' (side effects, reward hacking, scalable oversight, safe exploration, distributional shift).
quote: the problem of accidents in machine learning systems, defined as unintended and harmful behavior that may emerge from poor design of real-world AI systems.

role: Deep learning pioneer, University of Toronto / Google
title: Creative Destruction Lab talk: 'stop training radiologists'
summary: Hinton predicted deep learning would surpass radiologists within five to ten years; a famous, still-debated forecast.
quote: They should stop training radiologists now.

prediction.text: Deep learning will do better than radiologists in five years ('It might be ten years').

role: Neuroscientist (PhD, UCLA) and philosopher
title: TED Summit 2016: Can we build AI without losing control over it?
summary: Harris argued that any continued progress, not just exponential progress, eventually yields superhuman machines, and that our emotional response is dangerously inadequate.
quote: we have to admit that we are in the process of building some sort of god. Now would be a good time to make sure it's a god we can live with.

person: Katja Grace, John Salvatier, Allan Dafoe, Baobao Zhang, Owain Evans
role: AI Impacts / Future of Humanity Institute / Yale researchers

person: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
role: Google Brain / Google Research
title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Introduced the Transformer, an architecture built only on attention, more parallelizable than RNNs; it became the basis of GPT, BERT and every frontier model.
quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

role: Computer scientist, UC Berkeley; co-author of 'AI: A Modern Approach'
title: TED2017: 3 principles for creating safer AI
summary: Russell proposed machines that are altruistic, uncertain about human objectives, and learn them from human behavior, so they have an incentive to let us switch them off.
quote: you can't fetch the coffee if you're dead.

role: Physicist, MIT; co-founder, Future of Life Institute; author of 'Life 3.0' (2017)
title: TED2018: How to get empowered, not overpowered, by AI
summary: Building on Life 3.0, Tegmark argued humanity must move from learning-by-mistakes to proactive safety engineering as AGI approaches.
quote: if we win the wisdom race -- the race between the growing power of our technology and the growing wisdom with which we manage it.

role: Deep learning pioneer, Université de Montréal / MILA; 2018 Turing Award
title: Skeptical of superintelligence fears (Lex Fridman #4, 2018; BBC, Oct 2019)
summary: Before his 2023 turn toward x-risk, Bengio stressed near-term harms (surveillance, weapons, jobs, concentration of power) and doubted superintelligence was near.
quote: We are very far from super-intelligent AI systems and there may even be fundamental obstacles to get much beyond human intelligence.

person: OpenAI (Alec Radford, Jeff Wu, Dario Amodei, Ilya Sutskever et al.)
role: AI lab
title: GPT-2 and staged release ('Better language models and their implications')
summary: OpenAI withheld the full 1.5B-parameter GPT-2 over misuse fears, releasing it in stages through Nov 2019; the first major 'too dangerous to release' debate.
quote: Due to our concerns about malicious applications of the technology, we are not releasing the trained model.

role: Alignment researcher, OpenAI (later founded ARC)
title: What failure looks like
summary: Argued AI catastrophe would more likely be a gradual loss of control ('going out with a whimper') or influence-seeking systems ('going out with a bang') than a sudden Terminator-style takeover.
quote: The stereotyped image of AI catastrophe is a powerful, malicious AI system that takes its creators by surprise and quickly achieves a decisive advantage over the rest of humanity. I think this is probably not what failure will look like

role: Chief AI Scientist, Facebook; NYU; 2018 Turing Award (Zador: neuroscientist, Cold Spring Harbor)
title: Don't Fear the Terminator (Scientific American)
summary: LeCun and Zador argued AI never evolved a survival instinct, so intelligence does not imply a drive to dominate; sparked a public debate with Russell and Bengio over instrumental convergence.
quote: intelligence per se does not generate the drive for domination, any more than horns do.

role: Computer scientist, UC Berkeley
title: Human Compatible: Artificial Intelligence and the Problem of Control
summary: Book-length case that the 'standard model' of fixed objectives is dangerous and that provably beneficial AI must stay uncertain about human preferences; Bengio later said it raised his awareness of existential risk.

role: AI lab
title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
summary: A 175-billion-parameter autoregressive language model showed strong few-shot learning without fine-tuning, making the scaling hypothesis concrete.
quote: we train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model
